features: REVERSING AN INVOICE FROM A CLOSED YEAR NOW REALLY REMOVES THE EXPENSE IT CREATED — When an invoice arrives after the financial year has been closed, the program creates a dedicated expense chapter to hold it. Reversing the invoice used to leave that chapter standing: the actuals went on showing an expense no document justified, and the budget went on asking for that money as a requirement. The reversal now zeroes both, and the item stays visible at zero — it is not deleted, because the record of what happened must remain.

A PARTIALLY COVERED HISTORICAL INVOICE COULD NOT BE REVERSED AT ALL — When the amount exceeded the declared historical debt and the coverage was therefore split in two, the reversal stopped with a balancing error and nothing happened. The document stayed alive and the administrator had no way to cancel it. A defect present for several versions, not introduced by this one.

THE EXTRAORDINARY INSTALMENT PLAN NO LONGER OFFERS A CANCELLED INVOICE — The basket used to pick the expenses to share out kept offering reversed invoices, at their full amount and already suggested. Selecting them charged that money to the owners for a document that no longer exists. This also covers the current year's extraordinary invoices, which had the same omission.

THE EXTRAORDINARY PLAN'S BASKET NOW SAYS WHAT TO DO WHEN IT IS EMPTY — When there was nothing to share out it showed a line of text floating in an empty box. It now explains why it is empty and what to do — record an off-budget invoice, or pick another management — and when no management has been chosen yet it uses the same note as the opening-balances box, which already says the same thing. The card header now describes instead of instructing: it said «select the invoices» even when there was nothing to select. And the «legal shield» only appears when there is an invoice to authorise: with an empty basket it asked for the resolution behind an expense that does not exist, in a plan the program refuses anyway because it cannot be created without invoices. And in that state the card also drops its own header: what remains is a single box holding a sentence that explains itself.
RECORDED AMOUNTS DO NOT CHANGE — No migrations, no new ledger accounts, no existing entry rewritten. Whatever was already on the books stays identical.
